items.evidence: Notes cover the components ("Standard battery confirmed", "Chip-on-print"), wheel sensor cost ("~50x more expensive than a push button") and the voice recognition chip email, but never say the Industrial Designer presented the components. (In the transcript the voice chip was raised by the User Interface Designer.)
Notes say nothing about the User Interface Designer showing existing remote controls from the web.
Nothing about simplifying existing designs by dropping unneeded buttons or making it more ergonomic than the shown models; only the plastic cover point appears.
"Trend research from Paris and Milan: fruits/vegetables theme, spongy materials" and "Key priorities ranked: fancy look and feel > technological innovation > ease of use".
"fruits/vegetables theme, spongy materials" leading to "Banana shape selected" with "spongy outer cover".
"Component Decisions" and "Design Direction" sections list the agreed features.

Banana, spongy cover, backlit buttons, wheel on top, standard battery and chip all stated. But speech recognition is left as "Decision deferred: revisit after presentations" rather than being excluded; the transcript never brings it back and the agreed chip is the standard one.
"Industrial designer and UI designer collaborate on prototype prep" and "Evaluate product against user requirements".
"Industrial designer and UI designer collaborate on prototype prep".
"Evaluate product against user requirements: Check fancy look and feel, innovation, and ease of use against original user brief."
"Component Decisions" section and banana form decisions.
"Backlit buttons confirmed"; transcript: PM says "the button ar are lighted".
"Wheel on top, buttons on the side".
"Chip-on-print: specific chip identified, no issues" covers the standard chip, but notes leave voice recognition "Decision deferred" instead of stating it will not be included.
